blocking.section: Topology catalog (T4 chart object table) and Bootstrap and enrollment
blocking.issue: The Helm chart cannot bring up a three-voter Control Store unattended as written. The chart declares three identical ruralz-control StatefulSet pods, but bootstrap step 3 needs a human admin to create a join token in Ruralz Console before `ruralz control join` can run, and no first-admin credential is defined. If every pod runs `ruralz control serve` on an empty volume, each one generates its own CAs and elects itself leader. The result is three independent single-voter deployments with disjoint trust roots (split brain at install time).
blocking.evidence: "`ruralz-control` StatefulSet | Three pods, one per zone, each with a persistent volume; `OnDelete` updates..." and "3. **More replicas.** An `admin` creates a one-time join token in Ruralz Console Settings; `ruralz control join` redeems it over 8092 and the leader adds a voter." The CLI reference adds that join "runs on the new replica's host before `ruralz control serve`" with a token "issued by `/api/v1/replicas`".
blocking.fix: Add a chart row and a T4 paragraph saying that only ordinal 0 runs `ruralz control serve` on an empty Control Store. Ordinals 1 and 2 start with `ruralz control join` using a token from a bootstrap mechanism, and they never run serve on an empty store. Add an Open question (e.g., OQ-deployment-topologies-11) for (a) a chart bootstrap Job that mints join tokens through `/api/v1/replicas` with a one-time bootstrap admin credential from a Secret (proposed), or (b) a manual post-install step. Add a second Open question for how the first `admin` identity is created. Show the ordinal-0/ordinal-N split in Figure 7 or in the T4 text.

blocking.section: Topology catalog (T4 chart object table, Node StatefulSet and HorizontalPodAutoscaler rows)
blocking.issue: Nodes are deployed as an HPA-scaled StatefulSet, but the doc does not set podManagementPolicy. The Kubernetes default, OrderedReady, creates pods one at a time and waits for each to become Ready. A Control-mode Node is Ready only after Enrollment and its first Snapshot. So scale-out bursts are serialized, and one pod stuck not ready (token failure, Enroll lockout, or a Ruralz Control outage) blocks every later scale-out step. That coordination between Nodes contradicts P4.
blocking.evidence: "Node StatefulSet | A persistent volume for `${RURALZ_DATA_DIR}`, which rescheduled Control-mode pods MUST keep..." and "HorizontalPodAutoscaler | ... its minimum holds the headroom Node count"
blocking.fix: In the Node StatefulSet row, require `podManagementPolicy: Parallel`, with `updateStrategy` RollingUpdate and maxUnavailable held by the PodDisruptionBudget. State that one not-ready pod never blocks the creation of other pods. Show `Parallel` in Figure 4's Node StatefulSet label.

blocking.section: Topology catalog (T4) and Network and ports
blocking.issue: The T4 design leaves out the CRD conversion webhook that its dependencies say Ruralz Control serves. The Kubernetes API server must dial ruralz-control for conversion. That is an inbound connection with no port, Service, caBundle or flow row here. The release document also requires cluster-scoped RBAC on CRD status, and the chart's RBAC covers only Node secret reads. As written, the chart cannot serve a second CRD version, and it does not show that non-storage versions depend on Ruralz Control being available.
blocking.evidence: Configuration model: "On Kubernetes, CRDs serve all versions with one storage version and Ruralz Control serves the conversion webhook." Release doc: "CRDs serve every served version through Ruralz Control's conversion webhook, Planned (M2), so non-storage versions depend on its availability... needing cluster-scoped RBAC on CRD status." Deployment doc flow table lists only "CRD watch | Ruralz Control leader | Kubernetes API"; the Secrets row grants only "`get` and `watch` in the Node's namespace only".
blocking.fix: Add a chart row: a conversion-webhook Service on ruralz-control (port: new Open question, since pack 8.4 lists none; option (a) a path on 8090, (b) a dedicated port through a pack amendment), a caBundle from the server CA, and `conversion.strategy: None` while only `ruralz.io/v1alpha1` is served. Add a flow row 'Conversion webhook | Kubernetes API server | ruralz-control | T4'. Add an RBAC row for Ruralz Control: watch CRDs in bound namespaces, read cluster-scoped Environment and Cluster CRDs, update CRD status. State that CRD reads in non-storage versions fail while every replica is down.

blocking.section: Sizing defaults (Node container row) and Reference architectures
blocking.issue: The starting Node container memory is a misquote of Performance budgets. It drops the caveat 'or full state tables' and adds neither the default buffered-bytes budget nor the state tables. The doc also sets GOMEMLIMIT to about 90% of the container limit. A 2.2 GiB container then gives GOMEMLIMIT of about 2 GiB. The worst case at default limits is 1.83 GiB of TLS connections, 256 MiB base, 512 MiB of buffered bytes and about 475 MiB of state tables, roughly 3 GiB. That runs the GC continuously or gets the pod OOM-killed exactly at the 20,000-connection ceiling the row promises.
blocking.evidence: Deployment doc: "Node container | 4 vCPU (target) and at least 2.2 GiB of memory for 20,000 TLS connections without Plugins (target)" and "`GOMEMLIMIT` | About 90% of the container memory limit (target)". Performance doc: "Container memory for 20,000 TLS connections | 2.2 GiB or more (target), without Plugins or full state tables". Scalability doc: "Buffered bytes | 512 MiB proposed default (target)" and limits that "add ... about 475 MiB (target)".
blocking.fix: Restore the full caveat, then give a starting value that covers the default ceilings. For example: 2.2 GiB + 512 MiB buffered bytes + 475 MiB state tables ≈ 3.2 GiB (hypothesis), or 2.2 GiB with a lowered `limits.maxBufferedBytes`. Add one line: with Plugins, add the `limits.maxPluginMemoryBytes` cap (2 GiB default, WASM plugin system). Keep OQ-deployment-topologies-8 for measured values.

blocking.issue: The worked example gets State Store load from Node count times a generic per-Node coefficient instead of from request rate. S2 attaches `ratelimit` at the Gateway, and pack 8.8 says each locally admitted request runs GCRA. So 60,000 rps of S2-like traffic makes about 60,000 GCRA calls/s, and 78,000 with the 30% headroom, not 30,000. At the Scalability doc's 62.5% utilization of about 100,000 calls/s per shard (≈62,500), the headroom case needs two shards, not one. The example also carries S2's 32,000 rps saturation over to a `redis` Cell, but S2 is benchmarked on the `memory` driver. The per-Node figure is therefore a hypothesis, not a (target).
blocking.evidence: "State Store calls             6 × 5,000 = 30,000 calls/s, one shard with a replica  (hypothesis)" and "Per-Node capacity at 53% CPU  32,000 rps × 0.53 ≈ 16,960 rps per 4-vCPU Node        (target)". Performance doc S2: "`auth.jwt` and `ratelimit` at the Gateway, `memory` driver". Pack 8.8: "each locally admitted request runs GCRA in one Lua `EVAL` in the State Store".
blocking.fix: Replace the State Store line with calls = peak rps × blocking State Store calls per request, e.g. '60,000 × 1 GCRA = 60,000 calls/s; 78,000 with headroom > 62,500 per shard at 62.5% → 2 shards with replicas (hypothesis)'. Retag the per-Node line (hypothesis), noting that S2 runs the `memory` driver and that a `redis` Cell's per-Node throughput waits for an S2-with-redis or S5 measurement (Capacity planning).

blocking.issue: The doc presents 1,000 Nodes as the Cell split point but leaves out the Cell ceiling that binds first. The Scalability doc states that the 1,000,000 State Store calls/s per Cell ceiling binds at about 200 Nodes. An operator who follows T8 and the sizing table would grow a Cell to 1,000 Nodes and saturate its State Store at one fifth of that. Every Rate Limit would then fail open and every closed Token Budget would reject across the whole Cell.
blocking.evidence: Deployment doc: "A Cell reaching 1,000 Nodes (target) splits in two" and "Nodes per Cell | 1,000 at most (target)". Scalability doc: "At 5,000 State Store calls per second per Node (hypothesis), the 1,000,000-call ceiling binds at 200 Nodes, before the Node ceiling".
blocking.fix: Change T8 to 'A Cell splits in two when any Cell sizing ceiling would be exceeded: 1,000 Nodes (target) or 1,000,000 State Store calls/s (hypothesis), which binds first at about 200 Nodes of 5,000 calls/s each (hypothesis)'. Add a 'State Store calls per second per Cell' row to Sizing defaults, linking Cell sizing.

blocking.section: Reference architectures (RA-1) and Sizing defaults (Nodes per Cluster row)
blocking.issue: RA-1 puts three VMs in two zones. That means zones of two and one, and it has no autoscaler. Losing the two-VM zone leaves one Node carrying all traffic. The zone-derived CPU threshold (40% at two zones) holds only for equal zones, so a survivor at 3 × 40% = 120% CPU is overloaded. The same flaw carries into the sizing row, which quotes 'at least three in at least two zones' without the equal-zone condition.
blocking.evidence: "Nodes | Three VMs in two zones, systemd (T5)" and "Nodes per Cluster | At least three in at least two zones (target)". Scalability doc: "sized so that losing the largest zone keeps survivors under 80% CPU (target), which the zone-derived threshold ... enforces for equal zones".
blocking.fix: Change RA-1 to four VMs, two per zone, or three VMs across three zones. Add to the Nodes per Cluster row: 'with equal Node counts per zone; with unequal zones, size so the largest zone's loss keeps survivors under 80% CPU (target)'. Give RA-1's static peak CPU per Node explicitly (e.g., 40% or less at two equal zones (target)), since VMs without an autoscaler must be pre-sized.

blocking.section: Topology catalog (T10, Figure 6 caption and Outbound only bullet)
blocking.issue: The hybrid boundary claim contradicts Control plane and GitOps. The Ruralz Control builder runs an online Plugin check against allowlisted OCI registries whenever it records a Revision. A managed Ruralz Control therefore also dials the customer's Plugin registry. With a private registry that accepts no inbound connections, every build that references a Plugin fails. The doc covers only the Git case (OQ-deployment-topologies-10).
blocking.evidence: "*Figure 6: hybrid topology; only the Control Stream and Git reads cross the boundary.*" versus Control plane doc: "bld -.->|\"online Plugin check\"| oci" and "The online Plugin check dials only allowlisted registries..."; the same document's Figure 3 shows "r1 -.->|\"online Plugin check\"| oci".
blocking.fix: Add the OCI registry to Figure 6 with an edge from Ruralz Control labelled 'online Plugin check', correct the caption to 'the Control Stream, Git reads and Plugin registry checks', and widen OQ-deployment-topologies-10 to cover private registries: (a) a registry reachable from the managed side, (b) a mirror, (c) customer CI pushes with the check done in CI.

blocking.section: Bootstrap and enrollment (Enrollment per topology, closing sentence)
blocking.issue: The Enroll lockout is keyed by source address. That becomes a shared failure domain in the topologies this doc recommends. In T10 all customer Nodes dial out through one NAT, and many T4 clusters SNAT egress. Ten failed Enrolls from any Nodes (expired tokens after an outage, or reused tokens from StatefulSet init containers) lock out Enrollment for the whole Cluster. Meanwhile new Nodes without Last-Known-Good stay not ready. The stated mitigation does not follow, because pre-minting tokens does not reduce failures, and the per-source rate limit still throttles bursts.
blocking.evidence: "`Enroll` locks out a source after 10 failures in 10 minutes (target), so scale-out bursts SHOULD mint tokens before pods start." and "**Outbound only.** Nodes dial 8091 over mTLS, so customer firewalls open no inbound port."
blocking.fix: State that behind NAT or SNAT many Nodes share one Enroll source, so the lockout and rate limit apply per egress address. Add an Open question for keying the lockout by token or Cluster instead of source, or for an exemption per allowed CIDR. Replace the non-sequitur with a concrete rule: size the per-source Enroll rate limit above the largest expected scale-out burst per egress address (target), and alert on RZ-CP-001 bursts.

non_blocking.suggestion: 'about 30 s per 100-Node Cluster (target) plus bake' is SM-9's convergence figure and does not hold under `strategy: canary`. There, each of the three batches after the canary is gated for max(30 s, 3 × 15 s heartbeat) = 45 s (target), so a Cluster takes about 135 s plus `canary.bake`. With 300 edge Clusters at bake 15m, one promotion takes about 86 hours (hypothesis). Quote those figures.

Low-traffic edge Clusters under `strategy: canary` hit the 200-request minimum sample, and a thin canary gate pauses. That stalls the serial promotion of every later Cluster. Recommend `all-at-once` or file mode for low-traffic sites, or add the case to OQ-deployment-topologies-4.

Repeat Scalability's rule that autoscaled Control-mode Clusters SHOULD declare per-Node ceilings until OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-19 closes, because the published Node count rises at most 10% per minute after scale-out. Without it, an HPA burst over-admits by up to 20 × `requests` (hypothesis).

Qualify this. In file mode without a declared per-Node ceiling the ceiling equals the full limit (pack 8.8), so fail-open over-admission grows with Node count. Recommend declared ceilings for T2 Clusters.

'Across Regions only 8091, 8092, telemetry and configured Upstream traffic cross' contradicts RA-3's 'Backups copied to the second Region'. It also leaves out Git fetches and OCI pulls when the forge or registry sits in another Region. List them or say 'configuration and data-plane request traffic'.
Add the systemd equivalent of the Kubernetes termination rule: `TimeoutStopSec` MUST exceed the Drain deadline. Otherwise systemd SIGKILLs a draining Node.
With hundreds of Nodes, polling a registry reference is a fan-out onto the registry. Give a poll interval with jitter (target), and note the registry rate limits or a per-Cell pull-through mirror.

Show the basis for 4 GiB (hypothesis): 256 MiB of Snapshots in flight, per-stream send queues of 4 messages over 5,000 streams (shared encodings), the Raft log and the content store for the 50 retained Revisions per Environment. That way the F2 job measures the right terms.
The body is about 4,470 words against the 4,500 maximum. Write the blocking fixes compactly, as table rows or one sentence each, and do not delete earlier content to make room.
